metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly; apply a downward bias of 2–5% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — overcorrects toward recent lows; adjust forecast by adding 1–3% of recent 7-day average to counteract overcorrection.
- Model underestimates late-period drops (last 5–7 days of forecast) — especially after sustained high prices — apply a 2–4% upward bias to the final 5–7 days to account for volatility decay.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, model often fails to recognize the momentum — add a 1–3% downward adjustment to the forecast for the 3–5 days following the peak.
